title: Short Story and Poetry
notes: **Short story elements.** A short story works with plot, character, setting, theme and conflict; the plot moves from exposition through rising action and climax to resolution.
**Narrative voice.** First-person narration uses 'I' and limits knowledge to the narrator; third-person narration can be limited to one character or omniscient.
**Poetic form.** Poems are built from lines and stanzas with patterns of rhyme and rhythm (metre); free verse drops these fixed patterns.
**Figurative language.** Metaphor and simile compare, personification gives human traits, alliteration repeats opening sounds, and imagery appeals to the senses.
**Reading a poem.** Read aloud, paraphrase each stanza, identify the speaker and tone, then state the central message with evidence from the text.
